title: The Notebook and the Standard: Txillardegi, the Language He Rebuilt and the Organization He Named and Left
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: The Notebook from the Lithographer's Floor

stops.name: Antigua, Donostia, birth in the Gutenfelder house
stops.date_confidence: attested. Euskaltzaindia's official biography gives 27 September 1929; several agency obituaries printed 1927 and called him 84 at death, and that variant is not followed here. The Basque Wikipedia article supplies the street and house number (Amilibia, now Zumalakarregi, 579, the Gutenfelder house). The coordinate is the core of Antigua near Gaskuña plaza, not the house itself, which is not independently pinned.
stops.campa: On the twenty-seventh of September 1929, in the Gutenfelder house at number 579 of Amilibia street, in the fishing and working quarter of Antigua west of the city, a son is born to a family of the Donostia lower middle class. The father's people came out of Madrid to Tolosa before the Second Carlist War; the mother's, the Enparantza, come out of the Basque-speaking hill country around Oñati. In the house they speak Spanish. The mother uses Basque with her sisters and at the market. The boy does not learn it.
suggested_refs: Amilibia (now Zumalakarregi) street, Antigua, Donostia, and the Gaskuña plaza at the quarter's centre

stops.name: Antigua, Donostia, the month in bed and the grammar in the notebook
stops.date_confidence: year attested by txillardegi.wordpress.com/biografia; month not established and set to order the segment. The house name Casa Victoria, the grandfather's failed lithography workshop and the notebook made from its paper come from family-tradition material and could not be confirmed in either encyclopedia entry consulted; treated as [R].
stops.campa: He is seventeen and shut in the house for a month with an illness. To pass the time he begins to interrogate his mother about the language she has never taught him: how does one say this, why does the verb move here, what changes when the object is plural. He writes the answers down in a notebook made of paper from his grandfather's lithography workshop downstairs, a business that failed. By the end of the month the notebook holds a small grammar of Basque, assembled backwards out of one woman's speech. He still cannot hold a conversation in the language.
suggested_refs: The family lithography workshop in Antigua, source of the paper
sources: family-tradition material, unconfirmed in the encyclopedia entries consulted

stops.name: Parte Vieja, Donostia, the leaflets under the doors
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The anecdote, and his own dating of it as his first political action, appear only in the lead biographical material; neither encyclopedia entry consulted carries it. Month invented to order the segment after the notebook. Early nationalist sympathy is not itself in doubt.
stops.campa: The same year, at night, he goes through the old quarter pushing nationalist leaflets under doors. The party whose paper he is distributing is the one his generation will break with inside a decade, and the act is illegal in a city where the language on the leaflets is itself close to illegal. The notebook was finished in the same twelve months, in the same quarter of the same city. He counts the leaflets, afterwards, as his first political action.
suggested_refs: The old quarter of Donostia, ground of the clandestine distribution networks under Franco

stops.name: Donostia, the teachers found one at a time
stops.date_confidence: year attested by txillardegi.wordpress.com/biografia, which names both Jon Etxaide and Elbira Zipitria; month unknown and defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: He begins studying in earnest, and in a city where Basque is not taught he has to find the teachers one at a time. He meets Jon Etxaide, a writer working in a language with almost no readers, and Elbira Zipitria, who keeps a clandestine school in her own flat because the schools of the state will not have the language inside them. They give him a literature and a syntax he did not invent. They also give him the fact that other people are doing this.
suggested_refs: Elbira Zipitria's clandestine ikastola in a private flat in Donostia

stops.name: Bilbao, the engineering course and the impatient students
stops.date_confidence: year attested by txillardegi.wordpress.com/biografia and by eu.wikipedia ('studied engineering in Bilbao at the Technical Engineering School'); month unknown, defaulted to 01. The lead material's naming of an 'Academia Necoechea' specifically is unconfirmed. The 1948 Donostia meeting with Madariaga is dated in that traveler's own file.
stops.campa: He moves to Bilbao to read engineering. The city is heavier than Donostia, industrial, and full of students from every Basque province raised on a nationalism that lost its war before most of them could read. Among them is Julen Madariaga, a lawyer's son shipped to Chile as a child in 1937 and brought back to a grey country; the two have already met in Donostia the year before, in an older cousin's circle. What the students share is impatience. The party they were raised in waits abroad for the democracies to remember a promise.
suggested_refs: The engineering schools of Bilbao, recruiting ground of the Ekin circle
sources: julen_madariaga.journey.json, stop 'Donostia, the older cousin's circle'

stops.name: Plaza de la Constitución, Donostia, two groups speaking Basque
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction as to the exact date and square. The lead material places the meeting at a romería on the eve of San Sebastián Day, 19 January 1950; Jone Forcada's own obituary in Gaur8/Naiz, 15 November 2025, independently confirms that they met at a San Sebastián festival in 1950 without naming the square.
stops.campa: On the eve of the city's patron saint, in the arcaded square at the heart of the old quarter, two groups of young people drift together at a romería for one reason: both are speaking Basque, which in 1950 is a thing you can hear across a crowd. In the other group is Jone Forcada Adarraga. She will be his companion for sixty-two years and will keep the family fed through the long stretches when he cannot legally work. Later, on the French side of the river, she teaches at the ikastola at Hendaia.
suggested_refs: The Plaza de la Constitución, Donostia, and the San Sebastián Day romerías
sources: Gaur8/Naiz, obituary of Jone Forcada Adarraga, 15 November 2025

stops.name: Donostia, arrested for Jagi-Jagi
stops.date_confidence: year attested by txillardegi.wordpress.com/biografia, which pairs the first Basque-language articles with an arrest on a charge of belonging to Jagi-Jagi; month not established and set to order the stop after the January romería.
stops.campa: He has begun to publish articles in Basque, which is enough. The police take him and accuse him of belonging to Jagi-Jagi, the intransigent nationalist current whose name means Arise, Arise. It is his first arrest and it is short. Writing in the language is not treated by the state as literature but as an act. He is twenty years old and now a name on a list in Donostia; there will be a second arrest in ten years and a prison after it. He returns to the engineering course.
suggested_refs: The Jagi-Jagi current of Basque nationalism and its postwar clandestinity

segments.name: Ekin, the Duck, and the Four Initials

stops.name: Bilbao, Ekin is founded
stops.date_confidence: year attested; month unknown, defaulted to 01. The single-city framing is a simplification the sources do not support: es.wikipedia's article on Euskadi Ta Askatasuna describes Ekin as a merger of a Bilbao group with a Donostia group. Pin inherited byte-identical from julen_madariaga.journey.json, stop 'Bilbao, Ekin is founded'.
stops.campa: With Madariaga and a handful of other students he founds Ekin, which means to act or to set about. It is a study circle before it is anything else: Basque history, which is not taught, Basque grammar, which is not printed, and the political literature of small nations. The circle merges with the youth wing of the old party, quarrels with it about method for five years, and breaks away in May 1958. Nothing in the founding room is armed. There is a reading list and a mimeograph.
suggested_refs: Ekin's clandestine study papers, 1952-1958

stops.name: Zamora, two military services and a name taken off a house
stops.date_confidence: attested. txillardegi.wordpress.com/biografia records a first military service at Zamora in 1952 and a second in 1954, and dates the adoption of the pseudonym to 1954; eu.wikipedia gives the origin of the name as a house near the family home in Antigua. Month unknown, defaulted to 01, and the two Zamora periods are compressed into one stop.
stops.campa: Compulsory military service takes him twice to a Castilian garrison town four hundred kilometres from the sea, in 1952 and again in 1954. He is a Basque-language activist in a Spanish barracks, and the arrangement leaves him a great deal of time to read and to write. It is in the second of the two periods that he takes a pen name for his articles: Txillardegi, after a house standing near his family's own in Antigua. He signs it, and he will publish under it for the next fifty-eight years.
suggested_refs: The house called Txillardegi in the Antigua quarter of Donostia

stops.name: Ferrol, the last six months and Leturia's hidden diary
stops.date_confidence: attested by txillardegi.wordpress.com/biografia, which places the final six months of military service at Ferrol and the writing of the first novel there; month unknown, defaulted to 01. The 1955 Oiargi prize for the essay on Kierkegaard in Unamuno is from the same source and is folded into this stop.
stops.campa: A final six months of service, in the naval town on the Galician coast. He writes there a short novel in Basque, the diary of a man named Leturia who is dying and cannot decide what his life has meant. The models are Kierkegaard and Unamuno, on whom he had taken a prize the year before, and the Paris existentialists he is reading in translation. He is writing an unbeliever's interior monologue, in Basque, in a barracks. Nobody has done this. The literature of the language, at that date, is verse, sermons and the countryside.
suggested_refs: 'Kierkegaard-en hazia Unamuno-gan lore', Oiargi prize essay, 1955

stops.name: Donostia, the first modern novel and the Academy's card
stops.date_confidence: attested. Euskaltzaindia's official page dates his appointment as euskaltzain urgazlea, corresponding member, to 26 July 1957; en.wikipedia carries the publication of Leturiaren egunkari ezkutua in 1957 and its later standing as the first modern Basque novel. The two events are placed together on the Academy's date.
stops.campa: Leturiaren egunkari ezkutua is published and is at once called the first modern novel in Basque: interior, urban, unbelieving, written by a man who learned the language from his mother at seventeen. On the twenty-sixth of July the Academy of the Basque Language names him a corresponding member. He is twenty-seven years old. The clandestine organization he also belongs to will change its name within eighteen months, at a meeting on the Gipuzkoan coast.
suggested_refs: Leturiaren egunkari ezkutua, Euskaltzaindia, 1957; second edition Leopoldo Zugaza, 1977, with a new closing text by the author

stops.name: Deba, the duck rejected
stops.date_confidence: attested in es.wikipedia's article on Euskadi Ta Askatasuna, which places the naming at a meeting at Deba in late 1958 and names Txillardegi as proposing it, with Benito del Valle, Julen Madariaga and Iñaki Larramendi present. Historians treat the naming as a process rather than one dated meeting; participant testimony is the base of the account. Day set to 01. Pin inherited byte-identical from julen_madariaga.journey.json, stop 'Deba, the duck rejected'.
stops.campa: The group that has broken from the party meets on the Gipuzkoan coast to settle what to call itself. Aberri Ta Askatasuna is proposed, homeland and freedom, and the initials come out ATA, which in the Basque of Gipuzkoa means duck. He proposes Euskadi Ta Askatasuna instead, and it is taken. Benito del Valle, Julen Madariaga and Iñaki Larramendi are in the room. Whether a name is a founding, and whether this room or a letter eight months later is the beginning, is still argued by the people who were there and by the people who came after.
suggested_refs: Santiago de Pablo Contreras, 'Julio de 1959: el nacimiento de ETA', Historia Actual Online 48 (2019)
sources: Santiago de Pablo Contreras, Historia Actual Online 48:1 (2019), pp. 45-58

stops.name: Bilbao, the four initials and the notice to the lehendakari
stops.date_confidence: attested as to the date and the notice: his own internal document of 1971 states that on 31 July 1959 the divided Eusko Gaztedi changed its name and that Agirre was told the same day. His physical presence at the specific meeting is not documented, and the pin is the movement's Bilbao pin, inherited from julen_madariaga.journey.json, not a located room.
stops.campa: The divided youth organization formally adopts the new name, and word of the founding goes the same day to José Antonio Aguirre in Paris, the lehendakari who has spent twenty-one of his twenty-three years in office outside the country. The letter is a courtesy and a notice of succession. Aguirre will be dead in eight months, before the organization kills anyone. Txillardegi is twenty-nine years old and works as an engineer at a motor factory in Donostia.
stops.quote: On 31 July 1959, the divided Eusko Gaztedi decided to change its name: 'Euzkadi ta Askatasuna' [...]. The formation of the ETA organization was made known to [Lehendakari José Antonio] Agirre that same day.
stops.quote_source: Txillardegi, internal document, 1971, reproduced in Documentos Y, vol. I, p. 22; quoted in Santiago de Pablo Contreras, 'Julio de 1959: el nacimiento de ETA', Historia Actual Online 48:1 (2019), p. 52. English translation from the Spanish as quoted.
suggested_refs: Documentos Y, vol. I, p. 22, reproducing the 1971 internal account
sources: Santiago de Pablo Contreras, Historia Actual Online 48:1 (2019)
jose_antonio_aguirre.journey.json, stop 'Paris, the young men who will not wait'

stops.name: Antigua, Donostia, held incommunicado at the Civil Guard command
stops.date_confidence: attested by eu.wikipedia, 'Txillardegi', which places him incommunicado at the Guardia Civil command in Antigua after the August 1960 arrest, before the transfer to Martutene. Day unknown, defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: In August he is arrested a second time and held incommunicado at the Civil Guard command in his own quarter, a few streets from the house where he was born and from the house whose name he writes under. The interrogation of Basque suspects in Donostia at this date is conducted by men whose methods will be set out in court thirty years later. He gives nothing that produces further arrests. He is thirty. Outside, the organization goes on without him.
suggested_refs: The Civil Guard command post in the Antigua quarter of Donostia

stops.name: Martutene, the prison upriver
stops.date_confidence: attested by eu.wikipedia, 'Txillardegi': imprisonment at Martutene following the August 1960 arrest, released in November. Exact month of transfer not given; September set to order the stop between the arrest and the release.
stops.campa: He is held at Martutene, the prison on the Urumea above the city, until November. Imprisonment in 1960 is not yet the mass experience it will become for this movement; he is early. What the months settle is that he cannot go on living in Donostia writing under a pen name the police already have. Jone is outside with the children. When he comes out he begins, quietly, to arrange the crossing. He will not sleep another night in Gipuzkoa for sixteen years.
suggested_refs: Martutene prison, Donostia

stops.name: Irun and Hendaye, the crossing on New Year's Day
stops.date_confidence: the year and the destination are attested by txillardegi.wordpress.com/biografia and eu.wikipedia; the New Year's Day date and the specific border point come from the lead material and are not independently confirmed. The sources also disagree on the geography of the exile as a whole: one biographical page names France, Switzerland and Belgium, while every other account consulted names Hasparren, Paris, Belgium, Bordeaux and Hendaia and no Switzerland at all.
stops.campa: On the first day of the year he crosses the Bidasoa into the French Basque Country. In his own reckoning the exile is a short one, a matter of months until something gives in Madrid, and it lasts until 1977. Over its span the family will occupy sixteen different addresses in three countries. He crosses with Jone, the children, a novel written in a language nobody in France examines in, and an engineer's training that no French authority will recognize.
suggested_refs: The Bidasoa frontier at Irun and Hendaye

stops.name: Hasparren, mathematics at the Collège Saint-Joseph
stops.date_confidence: the teaching post at Hasparren from 1962 is attested by txillardegi.wordpress.com/biografia; the name of the school's director, Piarres Xarriton, and the 1965 dismissal come from the lead material and are not carried by either encyclopedia entry consulted. Month unknown, defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: In an inland Lapurdi town he is taken on to teach mathematics at the Collège Saint-Joseph, whose director is the priest Piarres Xarriton. It is the only steady work of the early exile and it lasts until he is dismissed in 1965. He teaches numbers in French to Basque children by day. At night he is writing about the letter h, and about which dialect's verb should stand in a common written language for a country on the other side of the hills that does not yet exist.
suggested_refs: Collège Saint-Joseph, Hasparren (Hazparne), Lapurdi
sources: lead material for the school and the dismissal, unconfirmed

stops.name: Bayonne, the Secretariat and the resignation printed in Enbata
stops.date_confidence: the founding of the Euskal Idazkaritza at Bayonne and his charge of its language work are attested by eu.wikipedia and txillardegi.wordpress.com/biografia; the resignation letter sent to Euskaltzaindia through Enbata is from the lead material and was not independently re-verified. Month unknown, defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: The Euskal Idazkaritza, the Basque Secretariat, is set up at Bayonne, and he is put in charge of its language work. The same year he sends a letter of resignation to the Academy of the Basque Language through the pages of Enbata, accusing it in public of inertia: four decades of an academy and still no agreed way to spell the language it was founded to defend. He has been a corresponding member for six years. The Secretariat calls its own congress for the following August.
suggested_refs: Enbata, the Bayonne abertzale paper, and the Euskal Idazkaritza papers, 1963-1965

stops.name: Bayonne, the congress of the twenty-ninth and thirtieth of August
stops.date_confidence: attested, and on two days rather than one: eu.wikipedia, 'Txillardegi', gives '1964ko abuztuaren 29 eta 30ean, Euskal Idazkaritzak Baionako Biltzarra antolatu zuen'. The stop is dated to the first day. Pierre Lafitte's patronage and the detail of the disputed letter h come from the lead material.
stops.campa: On the twenty-ninth and thirtieth of August the Secretariat holds its congress at Bayonne under the patronage of the philologist Pierre Lafitte. It adopts a practical written standard for immediate use: orthography, the disputed letter h, which verb forms, which dialect's endings. It carries no authority except that writers and papers begin to use it. Four years later the Academy will meet at Arantzazu, with a report from Koldo Mitxelena, and arrive at roughly the same place.
stops.quote: Is that mixture of sauces commonly called "richness" perhaps not the reflection of another, deeper error?
stops.quote_source: Txillardegi, 'Euskalkietatik euskerara', Zeruko Argia (1970); Spanish rendering quoted in Berria, 15 January 2012, republished sinpermiso.info, 25 March 2012. English translation from the Spanish.
suggested_refs: The Bayonne Congress resolutions of 29-30 August 1964; the Arantzazu congress of Euskaltzaindia, 1968

stops.name: Brussels, the United Nations passport
stops.date_confidence: attested by eu.wikipedia, 'Txillardegi': settled in Belgium as a stateless person with a UN passport. The stated cause, a French requirement that he leave the border departments, is from the lead material. Month set to order the stop after the Hasparren dismissal.
stops.campa: French authority requires him out of the border departments, and he goes north with the family to Belgium. He is registered there as apatride, stateless, and travels on a United Nations passport, the document issued to people no country will claim. He is thirty-five, with no nationality and no recognized qualification, and with the beginnings of a written standard for a language spoken by fewer people than live in the city he has just moved into. Waterloo is one of the addresses.
suggested_refs: The Nansen-type United Nations travel document issued to stateless persons
sources: lead material for the expulsion from the border zone and for the Waterloo address

stops.name: Brussels, Branka
stops.date_confidence: the launch of Branka in 1966 and its run to 1971 are attested by txillardegi.wordpress.com/biografia; month unknown, defaulted to 01. The detail that he wrote much of it under several signatures is from the same source.
stops.campa: From Brussels he launches Branka, a review for the exiles and for whoever can be got a copy inside. He writes much of it himself under several signatures, an old device of small emigrations, arguing two things at once: that the language is the substance of the nation and not its ornament, and that the organization he helped found is being taken over by people who believe the reverse. Branka runs until 1971. The print runs are small and the postage is the hard part.
suggested_refs: Branka, Brussels, 1966-1971, complete run

stops.name: Brussels, the letter of resignation
stops.date_confidence: attested by txillardegi.wordpress.com/biografia and en.wikipedia: he leaves ETA in 1967 after the Fifth Assembly's Marxist-Leninist turn, resigning by letter with several associates. Month unknown, defaulted to 01. His physical location at the moment of writing is inferred from the Belgian exile and is not separately documented.
stops.campa: At the Fifth Assembly the organization turns Marxist-Leninist and reclassifies the national question as a subordinate case of the class question. The argument he loses is the one he has been making since the notebook: that a people is constituted by the language it speaks and not by a position in the relations of production, and that an organization which forgets this will end up fighting a Spanish war in Basque. He is thirty-seven. He resigns by letter, with several others.
suggested_refs: The Fifth Assembly of ETA and the 1967 resignations

stops.name: Brussels, a prize and the news from the Aduna road
stops.date_confidence: the Txomin Agirre prize for Elsa Scheelen in 1968 is attested by txillardegi.wordpress.com/biografia; the killing of José Antonio Pardines on the Aduna-Villabona road on 7 June 1968 is attested by the Guardia Civil's own efemérides page. He was in Belgium and not present at either the checkpoint or the prize ceremony's country; the stop is his, at his own pin, on the date the news arrives.
stops.campa: He is awarded the Txomin Agirre prize for Elsa Scheelen, a novel with a Belgian woman at its centre, written in the language of a country he cannot enter. On the seventh of June a young man of the organization shoots a Civil Guard traffic officer named José Antonio Pardines dead at a checkpoint on the Aduna road, the first killing generally counted to it. He left the previous year over a question of doctrine. For the next forty-four years he will be asked to answer for what follows from this morning.
suggested_refs: Elsa Scheelen (1969); the Guardia Civil efemérides entry for 7 June 1968

stops.name: Pessac, the assistant at Bordeaux
stops.date_confidence: attested: txillardegi.wordpress.com/biografia dates the assistantship to 1970 and es.wikipedia confirms he taught at the Université de Bordeaux III Michel de Montaigne. Month unknown, defaulted to 01. Coordinate is the Pessac campus of Bordeaux Montaigne.
stops.campa: He takes a post as an assistant teacher at the university at Bordeaux. It is the first employment since he left Hasparren that uses what he actually knows. He is forty and begins again as a student of linguistics. The engineering is behind him and the novels are largely behind him; in front of him are phonology and the question of where the accent falls in a Basque word. An award reaches him this year from Caracas, and he cannot travel to collect it.
suggested_refs: Université Bordeaux Montaigne (Bordeaux III), Pessac campus
sources: lead material for the 1969 Andima award at Caracas, unconfirmed

stops.name: Hendaye, within sight of the country
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction as to the family's dates. Jone Forcada's obituary in Gaur8/Naiz, 15 November 2025, says the family settled at Hendaia around 1970 after constant displacement and dates her teaching at the Hendaia ikastola to 1970-1976; the lead material gave 1972-1977 and named the twins' return in 1972. Neither encyclopedia entry consulted names Hendaye at all.
stops.campa: The family settles at Hendaye, the last French town before the river, in sight of the country. Jone teaches at the ikastola here from 1970. The twins, Joseba and Jon, rejoin the household in 1972 after years with their grandparents in Donostia. These are the stable years of the exile, six of them at one address after nine at eleven. From the seafront he can see Hondarribia across the water, which is Gipuzkoa, where there is a file on him. He is writing, in these years, mostly about dialects.
stops.quote: Let it not be said afterward that these questions are trifles, since it is precisely these same things that lead our language to patois-ization and disaster.
stops.quote_source: Txillardegi, 'Euskalkietatik euskerara', Zeruko Argia (1970); Spanish rendering quoted in Berria, 15 January 2012, republished sinpermiso.info, 25 March 2012. English translation from the Spanish.
suggested_refs: The Hendaia ikastola, where Jone Forcada taught 1970-1976
sources: Gaur8/Naiz, obituary of Jone Forcada Adarraga, 15 November 2025

stops.name: Bordeaux, the account of the name written down
stops.date_confidence: the document is dated 1971 by Santiago de Pablo Contreras, who reproduces it from Documentos Y, vol. I, p. 22. The place of writing is inferred from the Bordeaux and Hendaia years and is not stated in the source; month unknown, defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: He sets down, in an internal document, his own account of how the organization got its name, twelve years after the fact and before any of the later versions have hardened. It is the earliest recorded telling by a participant, and a historian will find it in the movement's own published papers half a century afterwards. It is dry, dated and administrative. The anecdote about the Gipuzkoan word for duck, which he will tell for the rest of his life and which everybody will tell after him, is not in it.
suggested_refs: Documentos Y, vol. I, p. 22
sources: Santiago de Pablo Contreras, 'Julio de 1959: el nacimiento de ETA', Historia Actual Online 48:1 (2019), p. 52

stops.name: Paris, the licence in linguistics
stops.date_confidence: attested: eu.wikipedia gives a linguistics degree from the University of Paris and es.wikipedia confirms the licence obtained at Paris; txillardegi.wordpress.com/biografia dates it 1975. Month not established and set to the end of an academic year.
stops.campa: At forty-five he completes a licence in linguistics at the University of Paris, a credential assembled in fragments across fifteen years of displacement. He has read Jean-Paul Sartre and Albert Camus since his twenties, first in translation and then not; the novel he wrote in a Galician barracks was built out of them, and a preface he writes five years from now will open on Sartre's death. Now he is in their city, working on the sound systems of languages.
suggested_refs: Sorbonne, Université de Paris, licence en linguistique

stops.name: Irun, back across under guarantee
stops.date_confidence: the 1976 return is attested by es.wikipedia and en.wikipedia; txillardegi.wordpress.com/biografia dates the definitive return to 1977. The sources are not reconciled here. The brother's approach to the civil governor and the policeman's greeting are from the lead material only. Month unknown, defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: His brother obtains an assurance from the civil governor and he crosses back over the Irun bridge for a first protected visit, Franco two months dead. The policeman at the post reads his papers and says welcome to Spain, then corrects himself and says welcome to the Basque Country. He is forty-six and has been away sixteen years. The country he walks back into speaks less Basque than the one he left. Whether this year or the next is the real return the sources do not agree, and he crossed more than once before the file on him was closed.
suggested_refs: The Santiago bridge at Irun-Hendaye, crossing point of the return
sources: lead material for the border anecdote

stops.name: Donostia, phonology at the EUTG while the papers are settled
stops.date_confidence: attested by eu.wikipedia, which lists him teaching at Bordeaux and the EUTG across 1976-1983. Month set to the start of an academic year; the exact date of appointment is not given by any source consulted.
stops.campa: While the legal situation is being normalized he begins teaching phonology at the Jesuit faculty in Donostia. It is his first teaching post in his own city, at forty-seven, in the language he had assembled from his mother's answers in a notebook. He is a founder of an organization now killing at a rate the country has not seen, and a chief architect of the written standard being installed in the new ikastolas. He is also a man in his late forties looking for a salary.
suggested_refs: Estudios Universitarios y Técnicos de Guipúzcoa (EUTG), Donostia

stops.name: Donostia, Euskal Sozialista Biltzarrea
stops.date_confidence: the sources conflict and are not reconciled here: en.wikipedia states that in 1976 he and Iñaki Aldekoa formed the ESB, while txillardegi.wordpress.com/biografia and orain.eus place it in 1977. Month unknown, defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: With Iñaki Aldekoa he forms the Euskal Sozialista Biltzarrea, a Basque socialist assembly: independence, socialism, and the language written into the first article rather than annexed as culture. Whether the founding falls in 1976 or 1977 the sources do not agree. It is the first of four political formations he will join and leave across thirty years, each time on the same point, and each time earlier than the people who end up agreeing with him.
stops.quote: With a state, perhaps Basque will not be saved; but without one, it certainly will not be.
stops.quote_source: Attributed to Txillardegi. Basque original 'Estatu batekin, agian, euskara ez da salbatuko; baina estaturik gabe, ziur ezetz', eu.wikiquote (uncited); Spanish rendering in Berria, 15 January 2012, republished sinpermiso.info. Original occasion and date unestablished.
suggested_refs: Euskal Sozialista Biltzarrea-Partido Socialista Vasco founding documents
sources: orain.eus, 'Biografía: Txillardegi, vida dedicada al euskera'

stops.name: Donostia, Herri Batasuna
stops.date_confidence: the coalition was constituted after the Mesa de Alsasua of April 1978 and 1978 is the historically standard date; but en.wikipedia, the source usually cited for his participation, says 1977. The discrepancy is left standing. Day set to 01.
stops.campa: He takes part in the founding of Herri Batasuna, the coalition assembled after the Mesa de Alsasua, which will carry the votes of the movement's political wing for twenty years and will decline to occupy the seats it wins. A man who left the armed organization in 1967 over its abandonment of the language question now spends a decade inside the electoral coalition its prisoners' families vote for. Sources differ on whether he is in at 1977 or 1978.
suggested_refs: The Mesa de Alsasua, April 1978, and the constitution of Herri Batasuna

stops.name: Donostia, expelled from his own party, decorated for the grammar
stops.date_confidence: the expulsion from ESB and the Zilarrezko Lauburu for Euskal Gramatika are both dated 1980 by txillardegi.wordpress.com/biografia, without months. Sartre died on 15 April 1980 and the day is borrowed to order the stop. The preface to Paretaren kontra is cited by eu.wikiquote without a page or publisher and its date of composition is not established.
stops.campa: He is expelled from the Euskal Sozialista Biltzarrea, the party he founded three years earlier. In the same twelve months he is given the Silver Lauburu for Euskal Gramatika, the grammar he published in 1978. In April Jean-Paul Sartre dies in Paris, and a preface he writes opens by saying so. He had borrowed the diary form from Sartre and Unamuno at twenty-six, in a barracks on the Galician coast, for a novel about a man who could not decide what his life had meant.
stops.quote: Jean-Paul Sartre has died. And many of us have felt great sadness...
stops.quote_source: Txillardegi, preface to Paretaren kontra. Basque original 'Jean Paul Sartre hil da. Eta tristura handia senditu dugu askok...' cited by eu.wikiquote to this preface; the book itself could not be fetched.
suggested_refs: Euskal Gramatika (1978); the preface to Paretaren kontra

stops.name: UCLA, Los Angeles, a year of phonetics
stops.date_confidence: the California academic year is attested by txillardegi.wordpress.com/biografia and by eu.wikipedia, whose fetched summary garbled the institution's name; UCLA specifically comes from the lead material. Month set to the start of an academic year. The 1979 lectures on Jakobson, Chomsky and generative phonology are from the dossier chronology and are used here only as the content of his reading.
stops.campa: He spends an academic year in California studying phonetics and phonology, fifty-two years old, at a university where nobody there has heard of the language he works on. Two years earlier he had begun lecturing at home on Jakobson, Chomsky and generative phonology; now he is reading Noam Chomsky and Morris Halle in the place where the work is being done. To describe the accent of Basque he needs an apparatus built with no reference to Basque at all.
suggested_refs: The UCLA phonetics laboratory, early 1980s

stops.name: Zorroaga, Donostia, the chair
stops.date_confidence: the sources conflict and are not reconciled: txillardegi.wordpress.com/biografia gives 1982 for the appointment to the University of the Basque Country, while eu.wikipedia gives 1983-1999 for the Zorroaga faculty position. Month unknown, defaulted to 01. The emeritus designation at seventy is from eu.wikipedia.
stops.campa: He joins the faculty of the University of the Basque Country at Zorroaga, on the hill above the river, and teaches sociolinguistics and Basque phonology there for seventeen years. He will be made emeritus at seventy. The man who could not obtain a recognized qualification through fifteen years of exile now holds a post in the discipline, in his own city, in a university that did not exist when he crossed the Bidasoa. One source dates the appointment to 1982 and another to 1983.
suggested_refs: Zorroaga faculty, UPV/EHU, Donostia

stops.name: Bellaterra, the thesis on the Basque accent
stops.date_confidence: attested by Euskaltzaindia's official page and txillardegi.wordpress.com/biografia; both encyclopedia entries consulted said 'University of Barcelona' without specifying the Autonomous University, and the more precise institution comes from the lead material. The thesis is formally dated 1983 in some accounts and 1984 in others. Month unknown, defaulted to 01.
stops.campa: At the Autonomous University of Barcelona he defends a doctoral thesis on Basque accentuation: where the stress falls in a language whose dialects put it in different places and whose new standard had, until then, no answer to give. It is published the following year as Euskal azentuaz. He is fifty-four. The standard he helped write at Bayonne in 1964 as a dismissed schoolmaster he is now supplying, twenty years later, with the phonetics it went out into the world without.
stops.quote: Standard Basque is artificial; those who say it is artificial are right about that; it was never a dialect.
stops.quote_source: Txillardegi, interview by Gorka Bereziartua Mitxelena and Mikel Asurmendi, Argia 2104 / LARRUN 113, 30 September 2007. English translation of 'Euskara batua artifiziala da, horretan arrazoia dute esaten dutenek artifiziala dela, ez zen izan euskalki bat.'
suggested_refs: Euskal azentuaz (1984), from the Bellaterra thesis

stops.name: Palacio del Senado, Madrid, senator for Gipuzkoa
stops.date_confidence: the 1986 election on the Herri Batasuna list is attested by en.wikipedia and txillardegi.wordpress.com/biografia; the Spanish general election of that year was held on 22 June and the month is set from it, not from a source naming his own dates. A ministry archive photograph of 20 November 1989 identifies him among HB deputies and senators.
stops.campa: He is elected senator for Gipuzkoa on the Herri Batasuna list and takes a seat in the upper house in Madrid, for a coalition whose declared policy is not to occupy the seats it wins. He uses the mandate to talk about the language. His position, stated flatly and repeatedly for thirty years, is that a nationalism which is not first a struggle for the language has no content, and that the campaign running outside the building is not that struggle. He holds the seat until 1989.
stops.quote: Outside the struggle for Basque, Basque nationalism has no substance.
stops.quote_source: Txillardegi, Argia, 11 September 1983. Basque original 'Euskararen aldeko borrokatik at, euskal abertzaletasunak ez dik funtsik', cited with that date by eu.wikiquote; the Argia original itself could not be fetched.
suggested_refs: Palacio del Senado, Madrid; the Herri Batasuna abstention policy

stops.name: Madrid, the second term and the journal that keeps the count
stops.date_confidence: attested: es.wikipedia gives his Senate service for Gipuzkoa from 29 October 1989 to 12 May 1992, and txillardegi.wordpress.com/biografia dates the founding of Bat Soziolinguistika Aldizkaria to 1989 with his direction running to 2002.
stops.campa: He is returned to the Senate a second time, again for Gipuzkoa, and sits from the twenty-ninth of October 1989 to the twelfth of May 1992. In the same year he founds Bat Soziolinguistika Aldizkaria, a journal of sociolinguistics, and directs it for thirteen years, until 2002. The journal keeps the count, survey after survey: how many people actually speak the language, in which streets, to whom, in which of the two states, and at what age they stop. He is sixty.
suggested_refs: Bat Soziolinguistika Aldizkaria, founded 1989

stops.name: Donostia, Aralar
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction as to the date. en.wikipedia and orain.eus both place him in Aralar, a formation of the abertzale left that explicitly rejected ETA's violence; 2001 is the date carried by the dossier and month is unknown, defaulted to 01. Aralar was constituted formally in 2001.
stops.campa: He joins Aralar, a party formed out of the abertzale left which says plainly that the killing is wrong and must stop. He is seventy-two. He founded the organization it repudiates, named it, left it in 1967, and has spent thirty-four years being introduced by that fact in every hall he speaks in. The move costs him people who have called him a founder for four decades. The victims' associations do not regard the sequence as a redemption and say so.
suggested_refs: Aralar, founding declarations, 2001
sources: orain.eus, 'Biografía: Txillardegi, vida dedicada al euskera'

stops.name: Durango, the Argizaiola, and an honour declined
stops.date_confidence: the Argizaiola at the Durango fair is from the lead material only and is undated within 2004; the fair runs in early December, from which the month is taken. The Euskaltzaindia honorary designation of 26 November 2004 is attested by the Academy's own page, which also states that he declined the appointment.
stops.campa: At the Durango book and record fair, in the first week of December, he is given the Argizaiola prize. In November of the same year the Academy of the Basque Language designates him an honorary member and, according to the Academy's own record, he declines the appointment. The tributes printed after his death describe him as an honorary academic from 2004 and do not mention any refusal. Which is the true account, the Academy's page or the obituaries?
suggested_refs: Euskaltzaindia, register of honorary members (ohorezko euskaltzainak), 26 November 2004
sources: lead material for the Argizaiola, unconfirmed independently

stops.name: Amasa-Villabona, the farmhouse sold on one condition
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction throughout. The Bidarte farmhouse, the condition placed on the buyer, and the piano and library left behind come from the lead material only and are not in either encyclopedia entry consulted; no contract or document has been produced for the condition. Date invented to order the stop between the 2004 prizes and the 2007 departure from Aralar.
stops.campa: He and Jone sell the small farmhouse at Amasa-Villabona where they have lived since coming south. They set one condition on the sale and hold to it through offer after offer: the buyer must speak Basque. Eventually a buyer appears who does. It is the last property he owns. He is in his seventies and moving back into the old quarter whose doors he pushed leaflets under in 1947. The piano stays behind, and much of the library, which will not fit where they are going.
suggested_refs: The Bidarte farmhouse, Amasa-Villabona, Gipuzkoa

stops.name: Donostia, leaving Aralar
stops.date_confidence: the month is attested by eu.wikipedia ('2007ko maiatzean, ordea, alderdia uztea erabaki zuen'); the day is not sourced anywhere consulted and is defaulted to 01. The reasons circulating, an alliance with Ezker Batua and participation in an official act of solidarity with ETA's victims, are not carried by the source usually cited for them, which gives no date and no reason at all.
stops.campa: In May he leaves Aralar. The reasons given in circulating accounts are the party's alliance with a Spanish left formation and its participation in an official act of solidarity with the victims of the organization he founded; the sources that carry a date give no reasons, and the sources that give reasons carry no date. He is seventy-seven and has now left every political structure he has ever joined. In an interview that September he explains himself in a single sentence.
stops.quote: Conventional politics is not yet possible in this country.
stops.quote_source: Txillardegi, interview by Gorka Bereziartua Mitxelena and Mikel Asurmendi, Argia 2104, 30 September 2007. English translation of 'Politika konbentzionala ez da posible oraindik herri honetan.'
suggested_refs: Argia 2104 / LARRUN 113, 30 September 2007, the full interview

stops.name: Donostia, the last demonstration
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction. The tribute by Euskal Herrian Euskaraz after a national demonstration for Basque-language rights, and the recordings of one of his last public speeches, are from the lead material only and are dated no more precisely than February 2011; day defaulted to 01. The 2008 EAE-ANV Senate candidacy, blocked by the party's judicial suspension, is not staged as a separate stop.
stops.campa: After a national demonstration for the rights of Basque speakers, the organization Euskal Herrian Euskaraz honours him in the street, in the city he was born in. He is eighty-one and ill. Recordings preserve the tribute and one of the last speeches he gives in public. In October, nine months later and three months before he dies, the organization he named announces the end of its armed activity. The crowd around him in February is large and young, and speaks, for the most part, the standard he helped write at Bayonne.
stops.quote: If I have had that gift of foresight, I have had it in fact, not a priori.
stops.quote_source: Attributed to Txillardegi in an article translated from Berria, 15 January 2012, republished sinpermiso.info, 25 March 2012; no original document or date is given there. Tagged [R].
suggested_refs: Euskal Herrian Euskaraz recordings of the February 2011 tribute

stops.name: Donostia, death at home
stops.date_confidence: attested by Euskaltzaindia's official page, both encyclopedia entries, and orain.eus, which adds death at home around midday after an illness of almost a year. The quarter of the city is disputed: the lead material says the old quarter, and no source consulted confirms it. Pin is the general Donostia pin used across the corpus.
stops.campa: He dies at home in Donostia around midday on the fourteenth of January 2012, at eighty-two, after an illness of nearly a year. Sixty-five years earlier, in a bed a few streets from wherever this one stands, he had spent a month of illness asking his mother how to say things and writing the answers into a notebook. Between the two beds: a novel, a grammar, an orthography, two prisons, sixteen addresses, four parties. Which quarter of the city this house stood in the accounts do not agree on.
stops.quote: Txillardegi best incarnates the new Basque Country, the era usually called the postwar period [...] The great milestone, certainly, was the war. But it is astonishing how afterward [...] in language work, in literature, in our ideological struggle or worldview, in politics, the motives that will occupy us across fifty long years amid a thousand dark conflicts all appear together, in one clean stroke and with complete coherence, in him, as if in one brilliant new intuition of the future.
stops.quote_source: Joxe Azurmendi, 'Txillardegiren saioa: hastapenen bila', Jakin 114 (1999), quoted on eu.wikiquote. English translation from the Basque. This is a quotation about him, not by him.
suggested_refs: Joxe Azurmendi, 'Txillardegiren saioa: hastapenen bila', Jakin 114 (1999)
sources: orain.eus, 'Biografía: Txillardegi, vida dedicada al euskera'

stops.name: Donostia, the cloth off another man's coffin
stops.date_confidence: attested that he was cremated on 15 January 2012 and that his coffin was covered with the ikurriña that had covered Txomin Iturbe Abasolo's (txillardegi.wordpress.com/biografia, orain.eus). That the arrangement was made at his own prior request is asserted in circulating accounts but not by the source that records the cloth. Iturbe died near Berrouaghia, Algeria, on 27 February 1987 after deportation, officially in a traffic accident; accounts placing his death in a Guatemalan shootout are wrong.
stops.campa: He is cremated the day after his death. His coffin is covered with the same ikurriña that had covered the coffin of Txomin Iturbe Abasolo, an organization leader who died in Algeria in 1987 after deportation, officially in a road accident. Whether the arrangement was made at his own prior request is asserted in some accounts and is absent from the source that records the cloth. No source found names where the ashes went. A public remembrance act follows on the twenty-ninth of January.
suggested_refs: Txillardegi plaza (formerly Gaskuña plaza), Antigua, dedicated 2018, with the mural in his honour; the commemorative plaque at the Arantzazu sanctuary, Oñati, 2018
sources: orain.eus, 'Biografía: Txillardegi, vida dedicada al euskera'
